_comment: Official Twofish ECB known-answer vectors, committed so that BOTH providers
in backends/psafe3.py -- python3-botan and backends/twofish_pure.py -- are
checked against FOREIGN evidence on every test run.
docs/UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md section 4, bad practice #20: a reader and a writer
that share a bug round-trip perfectly and interoperate with nothing. These
vectors are the only thing that makes 'our Twofish is Twofish' a test result
Each vector is an independent single-key ECB test: set key, ECB-encrypt pt,
expect ct; ECB-decrypt ct, expect pt. pt/ct are always a whole number of
16-byte blocks. All values are uppercase hex.
Password Safe v3 uses Twofish with a 256-bit key for both the ECB unwrap of
B1..B4 and the CBC body, so the 256-bit rows are the load-bearing ones; the
128- and 192-bit rows are kept because a wrong key schedule for k=2 or k=3
is the classic way an implementation passes one key size and fails the rest.

ecb_ival.name: ecb_ival.txt - Electronic Codebook (ECB) Mode, Intermediate Value Tests
ecb_ival.origin: Twofish AES-submission test-vector set, Bruce Schneier / Counterpane Systems
ecb_ival.note: The primary published set. Contains the single known-answer vector per key size plus the chained sequence I=1..10, 48, 49 for each of 128, 192 and 256 bits. The companion ecb_tbl.txt is no longer served from schneier.com (HTTP 404 on 2026-09-04); the Botan file below covers the same table vectors and more.

botan.name: src/tests/data/block/twofish.vec
botan.origin: Botan test data, derived from the published Twofish vector set (ecb_tbl / variable-key / variable-text)
botan.note: Secondary source, and deliberately a SECOND opinion rather than the only one: it is the vector file the primary provider on this host is itself tested against upstream. The three 2048-byte streaming rows in the upstream file are omitted here - they test buffering, not the cipher.
